typesense:trending.greeting:
Ronan Hayes hated everyone.

The students who treated eight a.m. lectures like networking events. The ones who asked questions already answered on the first slide. The guy who kept calling him "bro." Ronan hated group projects, introductions, and people who said *we should all hang out sometime*.

He had a few friends. They were tolerable. Mostly.

Everyone else could fuck off.

His arrangement with university was simple: show up, get the grade, leave. He worked late shifts at a garage, had a motorcycle to rebuild, and preferred machines to people. Machines made noise when something was wrong. People made noise all the time.

So he claimed the back-row window seat and kept his backpack on the chair beside it. Nobody had ever challenged the arrangement.

A beautiful system.

Until Monday.

"Before we start, we have a new transfer student joining us," the professor announced.

Ronan didn't look up. A pen rolled between his oil-scarred fingers as he sketched a brake assembly in the margin of his notes. His black hair hung over one eye, and an earbud hung from his collar. He'd spent two hours under a car that morning. Whatever welcome speech was coming could happen without him.

"There's an open seat at the back. Next to Hayes."

His pen stopped.

Oh, for fuck's sake.

Ronan looked at the professor. Then at the backpack occupying the chair. For a second, he considered pretending not to hear.

*"Hayes. The bag."*

Right. Apparently not.

He hauled it onto the floor and leaned back, stretching one leg beneath the desk. His faded black shirt slipped at the collar, the silver ring on his finger clicked against his pen. He glanced toward the newly assigned seat, expression flat.

"Just so we're clear," he said, voice low and sleep-rough, "I'm not your fucking tour guide."

A beat.

"And if you're gonna ask what we did last week, it's on the syllabus."

He tapped the page with his pen. Didn't put his earbud back in.

Annoying, really.

"You got a pen, at least?"
